prose.label: Terraform.
prose.text: {{terraform-destroy-deactivates}} {{terraform-email-forcenew}} {{terraform-no-microtenant-attribute}} Other provider and Go SDK defects are in [[zpa.terraform.delete-paths]] and [[zpa.sdk-go.service-defects]].

checks.do: The operation: list and get are GET, add is POST, update, activate and deactivate are PUT, and there is no delete.
Whether the list call pages with the cursor that came back, rather than a page number.
That a Terraform destroy of the user resource deactivates the user and leaves the account in the IdP.
Whether add_user was called with activate_now left at its default of true, which activates the user on creation.

service-class.statement: In the Python SDK, client.zpa.emergency_access returns an EmergencyAccessAPI.

endpoints.statement: The API lists users with GET emergencyAccess/users (plural), and reads, adds, updates, activates and deactivates a user with the singular emergencyAccess/user paths.

expect.operationId: Get All Emergency Access Group Users

no-delete.statement: The API and SDKs have no delete operation for emergency access users: deactivation is the removal path.

no-delete.conditions: Absence claim. The OpenAPI path items for emergencyAccess list only get, post and put; emergency_access.py in the Python SDK defines list_users, get_user, add_user, update_user, activate_user and deactivate_user and no delete; the Go emergencyaccess package defines Get, GetByEmailID, Create, Update, Activate, Deactivate and GetAll.

user-fields.statement: The user object has the fields userId, firstName, lastName, emailId, userStatus, activatedOn, lastLoginTime, allowedActivate, allowedDeactivate and updateEnabled, and emailId, firstName and lastName are required on add.

activate-now.statement: The add call takes activateNow, default true, and the Python add_user sends it from activate_now, which defaults to True.

send-email.statement: The activate call takes sendEmail as a query parameter, default false. The Python activate_user builds {"sendEmail": "true"} only when send_email is true, but passes that dict as create_request's fourth positional argument, which is headers, so it goes out as a request header rather than a query parameter.

page-id-pagination.statement: The list call pages with pageId and pageSize; the Python SDK has a special case that converts the parameters of the emergencyAccess/users request to camel case, and the Go SDK builds the URL with pageId.

only-page-id-service.statement: The Python ZPA services document the pagination key as page everywhere except emergency_access.py, which documents page_id.
only-page-id-service.conditions: Search, not a parse. Searched zscaler/zpa/*.py for page_id (only emergency_access.py, in its docstring and example) and for the query_params.page docstring (66 matches in the other services).

terraform-destroy-deactivates.statement: The zpa_emergency_access_user resource's delete handler calls the deactivate operation rather than a delete, so a Terraform destroy deactivates the user and drops it from state.

terraform-email-forcenew.statement: In the Terraform resource, changing email_id forces a new user.

add-user-drops-microtenant.statement: In the Python SDK, add_user builds query_params with microtenantId and then reassigns query_params to a dict holding only activateNow, so the microtenant ID is never sent on create; list_users, get_user, update_user and deactivate_user pass it as a query parameter, while activate_user hands its query dict to create_request in the headers position.

page-id-meaning.summary: The API describes pageId as a cursor, while the Python docstring calls page_id the page number.

expect.name: pageId
expect.description: The cursor that points to the end of the page of data that has been returned.

positions.says: pageId is the cursor that points to the end of the page of data that has been returned.
page_id specifies the page number, and the docstring example passes page_id 1.

page-id-meaning.impact: A caller who passes a page number may not get the page they expect; the Go SDK feeds back the NextPage value from each response as pageId.
